what: The book-length works of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, gathered by work rather than by deposit. A work may have several editions and an apparatus of navigation maps, metadata packets and negation graphs around it; those are listed separately because a navigation map is not the book.
why: Assembled as a precondition for a heteronyms body. A body about non-singular authorship needs to know what each author wrote, and the registry stores that as deposits rather than as works — so editions, samplers, critical editions and apparatus all appear as separate rows with no field joining them.
method: Candidates taken from content_type declaring a book form, plus titles declaring a volume or cycle. Works separated from apparatus by hand, because the registry has no field distinguishing them. THIS IS AN EDITORIAL GATHERING, NOT A DERIVED ONE, and a different editor would group differently.

works.note: ELEVEN DEPOSITS AND NO EDITION. Parts One through Five are deposited, several in duplicate (#588/#589/#590 are all Part Two; #586/#587 are both Part Three; #591/#1341 are both Part One), alongside #584 A Commentary Tradition and #592 the Prolegomenon and Commentary Outline. THE OPERATOR'S RULE: if there is no full edition, it is an unrecovered work. There is not, so it is. This is the inverse of All That Lies Within Me — that work has an apparatus and no text; this one has the whole text in pieces and no edition.

unrecovered_note: TWO KINDS OF ABSENCE, AND THE INVENTORY DISTINGUISHES THEM. All That Lies Within Me has an apparatus and no text: a work-provenance record, a navigation map, a metadata packet, and no book. Combat Scholasticism has the whole text in eleven deposited parts and no edition. The operator's rule covers both: IF THERE IS NO FULL EDITION, IT IS AN UNRECOVERED WORK.
